A new executive order is changing how childhood vaccines are recommended, putting parents and doctors back in the driver’s seat.

The universal childhood vaccine list is being narrowed from 18 diseases to 11. The new core list covers measles, mumps, rubella, diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis, polio, Hib, pneumococcal disease, HPV, and chickenpox. The MMR shot will now be split into individual doses instead of one combined shot, and the remaining vaccines shift to shared clinical decision-making.

Joint Base Lindsey Graham stands as a fitting tribute to a man who dedicated decades to our state, our military, and our nation.
